transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-10-08 15:00 UTC | Duration: 47 minutes | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (SE), Marcus (SWE); Sarah (Head of ML), Tom (CTO), Lina (Platform), Devon (PM).

Summary: signoff on POC success criteria and acceptance tests, decide benchmarks and reporting.

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — this is Jordan from Redwood, and with me is Priya, our SE, and Marcus on infra. Quick check, can you hear us ok?
00:07 Sarah: Yep good here. Thanks.
00:10 Jordan: Great. Goal today is to lock the POC success criteria and acceptance tests so we can start the bench runs next week.
00:18 Tom: Sounds good. We're mainly focused on chat summarization and search re-rank embedding workloads. Want to make sure latency and cost are both acceptable, and that accuracy doesn't regress compared to our current service.
00:28 Priya: Perfect. We'll cover the workload sizing you sent and propose a set of benchmarks: latency p50/p95, throughput (req/sec), token cost, error rate, and a quality/regression test against your labeled prompt set.
00:40 Devon: For timelines — we are aiming to have pilot ready by end of October so product can start trials early Nov. Is that feasible?
00:47 Marcus: We'll see. Depends on dataset and infra access.
00:51 Jordan: Okay let's run through the workload: Lina, you shared a spreadsheet with ~10k chat sessions, 50k embedding requests, and expected concurrency of 30 concurrent users during peak. Does that still reflect reality?
01:04 Lina: Yes that's right; peak concurrency is 25-35. Average session length about 8 messages. Embedding size averages 384 tokens.
01:12 Priya: Good. For the POC we recommend two benchmark profiles: 1) interactive chat profile (low latency emphasis) and 2) bulk embedding profile (throughput/cost emphasis). We'll run those on both Redwood Hosted and Redwood Dedicated (your dedicated lanes) to compare.
01:25 Tom: On hosted vs dedicated — our security team prefers dedicated with VPC but we'd like the cost comparison. Also need to validate SSO and audit logs for the POC.
01:35 Jordan: Understood. For security, we can enable VPC peering and KMS integration on Private/Dedicated builds; for hosted we can provide SOC 2 attestation and a data retention agreement during the trial. We'll include the security docs in the follow-up.
01:46 Sarah: Ok specifics on the success criteria — what are you proposing?
01:50 Priya: Here's our proposed acceptance tests and thresholds:
01:53 Priya: 1) Latency: interactive chat p95 end-to-end inference under 350ms for single-turn generation (for typical 256-token outputs) — go threshold. For a stricter bar on Dedicated we can target p95 < 250ms as an aspirational win.
02:10 Priya: 2) Throughput: handle 30 concurrent users with 8 msg/session, which maps to about 40 req/sec sustained for the chat profile, no more than 5% request queuing.
02:21 Priya: 3) Embeddings: be able to process 50k embedding requests over a 2-hour window with average latency per embedding < 120ms (p95) and cost target per 1k embeddings under our estimate — we'll put the cost numbers in the SOW.
02:36 Priya: 4) Accuracy/quality: on the labeled prompt set (n=500), generation quality should not degrade more than 3% absolute in our key NLU metric (F1/intent accuracy) compared to your production baseline; also manual review pass rate >= 90% for critical flows.
02:55 Priya: 5) Reliability: error rate < 0.5% and no more than one outage incident during the test window.
03:03 Sarah: A couple questions — first, p95 350ms seems aggressive compared to our current infra which is around 500ms. Is that realistic?
03:11 Priya: It's achievable on many models with optimized kernels and prefix caching; for longer contexts we'd expect higher numbers. That's why we want to run the actual workload against your sample data. Also for Dedicated you often see lower tail latency due to pinned capacity.
03:24 Tom: About accuracy — how will we measure the 3% degradation? Will Redwood run evaluation or do we provide labels?
03:30 Jordan: We'll do both — you provide the labeled set and expected outputs. We'll run automated evals comparing Rouge/F1/intent metrics and include sampled human review for edge cases. We'll surface diffs in the Redwood Console and in the shared Google Sheet.
03:43 Lina: Reporting format — we want CSV exports and a dashboard snapshot weekly. Also need raw request/response samples for 50 failed cases.
03:52 Marcus: We can push per-route logs, token-level latency breakdowns, and sample payload exports. We'll anonymize PII if present.
03:59 Devon: For go/no-go decision, who signs off? Product + ML team?
04:03 Tom: CTO and Head of ML sign off. Devon to coordinate product acceptance.
04:08 Sarah: Also call out security acceptance — our security engineer will check audit logs and KMS integration; if anything fails there, that can block the POC.
04:16 Jordan: Noted. We'll include that as a gating acceptance test.
04:20 Priya: To be explicit, proposed go/no-go thresholds:
04:23 Priya: - Go if chat p95 <= 350ms AND throughput >= 40 req/sec AND quality degradation <= 3% AND error rate <= 0.5% AND security checklist pass.
04:35 Priya: - No-go if any of the critical items (latency, quality, security) fail to meet the go thresholds. Minor misses (small delta in throughput or cost slightly above target) can be discussed.
04:46 Sarah: For the cost piece can you give a rough number today?
04:49 Jordan: We'll include estimated cost-per-1k-tokens and per-embedding numbers in the proposal — rough ballpark: Hosted may be ~20-30% higher than Dedicated for heavy throughput but has faster onboarding. But we'll produce concrete USD numbers in the SOW.
05:02 Devon: About the benchmark runs — what's the plan and what do you need from us?
05:06 Priya: We need the sample workload, an access account or instructions to run tests against your dev VPC (if Dedicated) or we'll run runs from Redwood Hosted using synthetic load matching your dataset. Also need the labeled eval set for quality checks.
05:19 Lina: We'll provide a GCS bucket with the samples and a small script to replay sessions. We'll add service account with limited rights.
05:26 Jordan: Great. We'll also provide a checklist for the runtime config: model selection (we'll propose a comparable open model), quantization level (8-bit), batching settings, prefix caching settings, and sequence length assumptions.
05:38 Tom: On model selection, are you suggesting we deviate from our internal fine-tuned model?
05:42 Priya: For the POC we can test with both — an open model (for baseline perf/cost) and a tuned version if you want to bring it. There may be extra setup for model onboarding on your side.
05:54 Sarah: What about metrics reporting cadence? Weekly is ok but we want daily smoke reports during the active benchmark window.
06:01 Jordan: We can do daily smoke, full report weekly, and an executive summary after the run. We'll populate the Google Sheet with per-route numbers and link the Redwood Console dashboard for drilldowns.
06:12 Devon: If the POC passes, what are typical next steps for Dedicated procurement?
06:16 Jordan: Typically you move to a 3-month pilot with Reserved capacity commits or a production ramp with a Dedicated contract; we'll share typical contract terms in the proposal.
06:24 Sarah: Any concerns about data residency? Our EU customers must remain in eu-west1.
06:29 Marcus: We can pin the Dedicated nodes to eu-west1 and run the benchmark there; hosted also has region options but we'll need to validate latency.
06:37 Priya: One more thing — acceptance test artifacts: we will produce a zip with the following after the run: metrics CSVs, top 50 diffs, 50 failed sample payloads, model config used, and the Redwood Console snapshot. That will be the canonical artifact for signoff.
06:51 Tom: That works. Can you also include a short script to reproduce the bench run? Our infra team likes that.
06:57 Marcus: We'll provide the replay script and infra steps; it's usually a small Python harness.
07:02 Jordan: Ok timeline recap — Lina to deliver data by 2025-10-13, Priya to run bench runs week of 2025-10-20, preliminary results by 2025-10-24, review and signoff meeting 2025-10-28. Does that match everyone's expectations?
07:16 Sarah: Yes that works.
07:19 Devon: We will aim to review labeling and acceptance prompts by 2025-10-17.
07:24 Jordan: Great. Anything else on success criteria?
07:26 Sarah: One last ask — in the acceptance tests can you include a human evaluation rubric for the manual review? We want to ensure consistent pass/fail across reviewers.
07:33 Priya: Absolutely — we'll include a rubric with example pass/fail cases and scoring guidelines (0-3 scale per criterion).
07:40 Jordan: Alright, quick recap of action items — we'll send the SOW/proposal and security docs, you'll provide dataset and access, we'll run benchmarks and produce the reporting artifacts.
07:51 Tom: Thank you, looking forward.
07:54 Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark window and the review meeting.
07:59 Sarah: Bye.
08:01 [call ends]

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings ("KV cash" for KV cache) — minor. References: Redwood Console dashboard, Redwood Dedicated, VPC, KMS, SOC 2. Shared artifacts: SOW draft (link placeholder), security docs (link placeholder), benchmark spreadsheet (Google Sheet link placeholder).
